title: A lookup tool for LLM agents
one_liner: A tool-calling function `threatcluster_lookup(query)` for LLM agents.
what_you_get: Wraps the unified search endpoint as a plain Python function that returns a compact, JSON-serialisable answer: a one-line summary, the matching clusters with scores, the matching entities and dark-web groups, and a `citations` list of ThreatCluster URLs the model can quote. walkthrough.title: Get a key
walkthrough.text: Sign in, open Settings, then API & Feeds, and select Generate API key. The key is shown once, so copy it. Every account has one and the free key covers this recipe.

image.alt: The ThreatCluster API page with the Get a free key button and the quick start, which begins with creating a key
image.caption: The API page. The key itself is created in Settings, under API & Feeds.

walkthrough.title: Download the script and set the key
walkthrough.text: The script is one file with one dependency. It reads the key from the environment, so the key never goes into the file.

walkthrough.title: Run it
walkthrough.text: Run from the command line, the script prints the JSON a model would receive from the tool: a one-line answer, the matching incidents, and a list of citation links.

image.alt: A terminal running the tool with the query citrix netscaler and printing JSON with an answer line and the first incident, including its title, score of 80 and summary
image.caption: Run on 29 September 2026. Five incidents matched. The answer line names the highest-scoring one.

walkthrough.title: Follow a citation
walkthrough.text: Every incident in the result carries its link, so the model can cite what it used and a person can check it.

image.alt: The ThreatCluster incident page for the Citrix NetScaler zero-days confirmed by CISA, with key points, the summary and 13 extracted entities
image.caption: The first citation from the run above.

walkthrough.title: Register it with a model
walkthrough.text: Import the function and its schema from the file. The same schema works for OpenAI and for Claude, which names the field input_schema.
walkthrough.commands:
# OpenAI
tools=[{"type": "function", "function": TOOL_SCHEMA}]

# Claude
tools=[{"name": TOOL_SCHEMA["name"], "description": TOOL_SCHEMA["description"],
        "input_schema": TOOL_SCHEMA["parameters"]}]

# either: on a tool call, return this as the tool result
json.dumps(threatcluster_lookup(**args))

title: CVE triage: KEV and EPSS filter
one_liner: From a list of CVE ids, keep only the ones that matter right now.
what_you_get: Reads CVE ids from a file (or stdin), looks each one up, and prints only those that are in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog OR have an EPSS score at or above a cut-off, with CVSS severity, EPSS, a known-public-exploit flag and the ThreatCluster page. Ids the API does not know (404) are listed at the end so nothing silently disappears.
